title: Mie Goreng
subtitle: indonesian fried noodles
excerpt: Mie goreng is Indonesian stir-fried noodles tossed in a wok with chicken, cabbage, and a savoury sauce of soy, oyster sauce, and sesame oil. It is a close sibling of nasi goreng and just as quick to make. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Mie goreng means fried noodles in Indonesian. It is eaten across Indonesia and is also popular in Malaysia and Singapore. Like nasi goreng, it is eaten at any time of day.

glossaryTerms.definition: Indonesian stir-fried noodles. The name means fried noodles. It is made with egg noodles or rice noodles and seasoned with soy and oyster sauce.
A thick, savoury sauce made from oyster extracts, sugar, and salt. It adds depth and a slight sweetness to stir-fried noodle dishes.

content.text: follows the same formula as nasi goreng but uses noodles instead of rice. A very hot wok and pre-mixed sauce are the two things that make it work. Serves 4.

items.prepNote: or egg noodles; soaked in hot water until just pliable if dried, then drained

content.text: Mix the soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sesame oil together in a small bowl and set aside.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat until smoking. Add the shallots, garlic, and chilli. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the chicken. Stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes until cooked through.
Add the noodles. Toss and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Let them sit against the hot wok for 20 seconds at a time to pick up some colour.
Add the cabbage and bean sprouts. Pour over the sauce. Toss everything together for 2 minutes.
Taste and adjust with more soy if needed. Serve topped with spring onion.

attrs.solution: Toss soaked dried noodles in a teaspoon of oil before cooking. Separate fresh noodles by hand before they go into the wok.
The oyster sauce and soy together can be very salty. Start with less and add more at the end once you taste.

attrs.problem: The cabbage is releasing too much water.
attrs.solution: Shred it finely and cook it over the highest heat so the moisture evaporates quickly rather than making the noodles wet.

content.text: Mie goreng is eaten across Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore. It is a street food staple and home kitchen standard. The dish varies by region with some versions adding prawns or tofu. In the Netherlands, a packaged version called Indomie mie goreng is one of the best-selling instant noodle products in the world.
